segments.text: A clock above the stove
had stopped at 2.13
Your coffee cup
was waiting where it
always used to be
Message on the
machine said you were
heading home
I heard you tie a little
lap, then I heard the
tongue
September 11th
came down without a warning bell red light forged the hallway when the sheriff came to tell
wood drumming crossed the center line and tore our world apart
i stood inside the house and felt the silent start
i ask the empty rooms what mercy is supposed to do when every chair remembers someone taken by
the truth i know that hate won't wake you but i hold it like a rail because the floor beneath me
disappears when i say
9-11 again, 9-11 again, 9-11 again, 9-11 again, 9-11 again, 9-11 again, 9-11 again
The calendar turns over but the night refuses to end
There were drawings on the icebox, yellow suns and purple rain
A jacket by the doorway with a crayon and a chain
your wedding ring came home to me inside a plastic sleeve the smallest things have weighed
enough to bring me to my knees they tell me he was sorry when the courtroom settled down
he couldn't raise his eyes while every camera turned around i wanted him to carry every name
beneath his skin.
I wanted him to wake each night inside the wreck
he made there.
But anger is a tenant that keeps changing every lock
It drinks the morning slowly and it watches every clock
i feed it all the questions that no witness can resolve why his hands were on that wheel
why mine weren't there at all i took the extra shift that night i said we'd meet the pain
you told me don't be late and drove the children on your way now guilt repeats that doorway like
a film i cannot mend if i had just been home with you then where would sorrow end
9 11 again 9 11 again 9 11 again 9 11 again 9 11 again every siren finds the road and drives me
backward through the red your sister says forgiveness isn't pardon or release it doesn't
call the damage small address the wrecking piece it may be setting down the glass before it cuts
me through it may be saying i survived without betraying you
I wrote him seven letters
Then I burned them one by one
The eighth one only said your names
And what his choice had done
The ninth began, I hate you
And the tenth began, I grieved
The last remains unfinished
I am trying still to live
I was not the headlights
I was not the drink
I was not the center light
I could not make Tom Blaine
I was working for our future
I did not shoot your end
Still the old accusation circles through my head
9-11 again, 9-11 again, 9-11 again
9-11 again, 9-11 again, 9-11 again
Tonight I set four places, then I put three plates away
i opened up the curtains at the breaking of the day your rose is tough the winter but one branch
is showing green a stubborn little answer in the yard where grief has been i cannot give him mercy
like a judge with lifted hands i cannot force my heart to go where it still cannot stand
But I can stop condemning that man working late downtown
Who thought he served his family and was absent when night came down
9-11 again, 9-11 again, 9-11 again
9-11 again
The words are still a wound, but they no longer own my name
I speak your names at sunrise, every syllable held clear
My love was in that house with you, though I could not be there
I may never call in mercy, I may never understand
But I release my own throat from the judgment of my hands
The road keeps what it took from me, the morning still comes in
I'll leave the porch black burning
Then I finally step within
